before: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, 'Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!'
after: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased they would sigh, 'Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!'
reason: The grammatical subject continues the eunuchs ordered to flatter the prince in s0015; 每見…輒歎 is their speech, not Empress Jia speaking personally.

before: Yet he ran a palace bazaar—himself butchering, selling ale, and weighing coin.
after: Yet he ran a palace bazaar, having others butcher and sell ale while he weighed the goods himself with exact accuracy.
reason: 使人屠酤 assigns butchering and selling to other people; 手揣斤兩 says he personally gauged weights, not that he weighed coin.

before: He drew double stipends to bankroll favorites.
after: He habitually drew two months of the palace allowance in advance to supply his favorites.
reason: 探取二月 describes drawing two months in advance, not a doubling of the regular stipend.

before: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Prince Chengdu of Ying saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
after: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
reason: 成都王 is the title Prince of Chengdu and 穎 is the given name Ying; the old word order reverses that relationship.

after: He had not yet seen Your Highness and feared that drinking this would leave him incapacitated.
reason: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒 refers to not yet seeing the addressee and fear of intoxication; it says nothing about copying a document.

before: Lü jailed and starved Yu; sympathizers smuggled food over walls.
after: Lü reported to Liu Zhen, who moved Yu to a small compound and cut off all food; palace sympathizers still passed food to him over the walls.
reason: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙 explicitly switches the acting subject from Sun Lü to Liu Zhen for moving and starving the prince.

before: She posed as hoping Yu could repent posthumously.
after: She claimed she had hoped Yu would take the lesson deeply to heart, reconsider his filial duty, and bow in repentance to restore his name.
reason: The memorial recalls Jia’s claimed earlier hope for Yu to repent and rectify his standing; it does not claim that repentance could occur after his death.

before: Huguan's steadfast lord—autumn-thousand years awakened self.
after: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
reason: 壺關 and 千秋 are historical allusions, not a steadfast lord and autumn-thousand years. Pinned Hanshu073 s0031/s0062 and Hanshu077 s0072–77 establish the remonstrances and the emperor’s realization.

after: The elder of Huguan spoke up for the wronged prince; Qianqiu made the emperor see his error.
reason: The parallel allusions concern remonstrance for the wronged Han crown prince. Exact pinned Hanshu witnesses are sealed separately; this restores the named Qianqiu instead of a generic summary.
